These diagrams use JSXGraph. One supplies a mathematics task; the other supplies
a language task with no Python execution. Both use the same feedback settings.

::: {.callout-note .example-author-notes}
### For course authors

The diagrams are drawn in sandboxed JSXGraph frames. The math task provides its
relevant lengths as text as well as on the diagram. The language activity's
hidden reviewer criteria describe the two figures, so feedback does not have to
infer geometry from a screenshot or read source JavaScript.
:::

### 1. Find a length

::: {#task-jsxgraph-math .example-learner-task}
**Your task**

The right triangle has perpendicular sides of lengths 3 and 4. Find the length
of the sloping side. A draft answer is already entered; finish or correct it.

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="assessment-triangle" width="600" height="340" style="max-width:100%; border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:8px;"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
  boundingbox: [-1, 5, 6, -1], axis: false, keepaspectratio: true,
  showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false
});
var a = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: 'A', fixed: true});
var b = board.create('point', [3, 0], {name: 'B', fixed: true});
var c = board.create('point', [3, 4], {name: 'C', fixed: true});
board.create('polygon', [a, b, c], {fillColor: '#dbeafe', fillOpacity: 0.5});
board.create('text', [1.4, -0.45, '3'], {fixed: true});
board.create('text', [3.3, 2, '4'], {fixed: true});
board.create('text', [0.8, 2.2, '?'], {fixed: true});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| label: integration-jsxgraph-length
#| context: none
The right triangle has perpendicular sides 3 and 4. The sloping side has length _[5].
```
:::

### 2. Name the shapes in German

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="assessment-german-shapes" width="680" height="320" style="max-width:100%; border:1px solid #ddd; border-radius:8px;"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
  boundingbox: [-4, 2.3, 4, -2.3], axis: false, keepaspectratio: true,
  showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false
});
board.create('circle', [[-2, 0], 1], {
  strokeColor: '#2563eb', fillColor: '#dbeafe', fillOpacity: 0.7, fixed: true
});
board.create('polygon', [[1, -1], [3, -1], [3, 1], [1, 1]], {
  vertices: {visible: false, fixed: true}, borders: {strokeColor: '#16a34a'},
  fillColor: '#dcfce7', fillOpacity: 0.7, fixed: true
});
board.create('text', [-2.1, -1.5, 'A'], {fixed: true});
board.create('text', [1.9, -1.5, 'B'], {fixed: true});
```

::: {.ai-feedback #german-shapes profile="language-quality" response-language="de" feedback-language="en" learner-level="German course 1" context="none"}
**Your task**

Wie heißen die Formen A und B auf Deutsch? Schreibe den Namen mit dem bestimmten
Artikel. Complete or correct the two German names in the draft.

::: {.feedback-starter}
A: der Kreis
B: das Rechteck
:::

::: {.feedback-criteria}
Figure A is a circle; figure B is a square. The expected German names with
articles are "der Kreis" and "das Quadrat". Review the shape names and articles
at beginner level. A square is a special rectangle, but this task asks for the
more precise name. Do not rewrite unrelated text or invent visual details.
:::
:::
